source.title: VReST: Enhancing Reasoning in Large Vision-Language Models through Tree Search and Self-Reward Mechanism
source.authors: Congzhi Zhang; Jiawei Peng; Zhenglin Wang; Yilong Lai; Haowen Sun; Heng Chang; Fei Ma; Weijiang Yu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses additional inference-time search as a way to improve multimodal reasoning and cites inference-scaling work as motivation. It does not test the claim’s pretraining-loss power laws or compute-optimal training allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports multimodal task accuracy as MCTS iterations increase. This is test-time accuracy scaling, not held-out pretraining loss scaling, parameter/token/compute scaling of training runs, or a compute-optimal training split. Figure 4’s comparisons against other methods are not cataloged as claim-version results; the iteration trends are retained as related findings outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a training-free MCTS method for vision-language reasoning and reports task accuracy against test-time iterations, plus a Qwen2.5-VL-3B vs Qwen2-VL-7B comparison. It never varies training parameters, tokens or compute, and never measures pretraining loss or fits a power law. Its 'test-time scaling law' is a related but different construct, and the iteration results mainly show its own method's performance against baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors claim state-of-the-art accuracy among training-free prompting methods, and say gains grow with MCTS iterations, which they frame as validating test-time scaling laws for multimodal tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses inference-time MCTS and self-rewarding to improve task-answer accuracy; it does not measure pretraining loss across parameter, token, or training-compute scales.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-time accuracy trend varies with MCTS iteration count and is plotted separately for MathVista, MathVision, and CharXiv. Figure 4 also compares different methods, whose x-axes correspond to different sampling or search hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: VReST-Vote accuracy rises with MCTS iterations (K=2 to 10) on MathVista, MathVision and CharXiv with Qwen2-VL-7B. The authors call this a 'better test-time scaling law', but no functional fit is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time search iterations improve multimodal reasoning accuracy.

record.problems: The scaling results are provided as plots without exact values in the text or reported uncertainty. The authors state that they evaluated VReST only on Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct and note computational cost and dataset dependence.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.7, Figure 4 compares CoT-Vote, Best-of-N, ToT, and VReST-Vote. The comparison values are not separately recorded because they do not measure the claim’s listed pretraining-scaling versions. Benchmark accuracy tables and ablations are also omitted because they do not test those versions.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
Effects of architecture shape at a fixed parameter count.
Power laws in other modalities or training regimes. There is no training-loss scaling here.
Downstream performance versus model scale. Only two model sizes (3B and 7B) from different families and generations are run, as a robustness check, with no scaling trend.
Dependence of fitted exponents on setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix F (Qwen2.5-VL-3B) shows the method still works on a smaller model. That result is not a scaling test, because it involves a different model generation, only two points, and no loss measure. 'Scaling law' here refers to inference-time scaling, not the Kaplan or Hoffmann training laws.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or training compute.
Whether power-law fits from small pretraining runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation for a fixed training compute budget.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices on loss at fixed parameter count.
The same power-law form for held-out pretraining loss in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream-task performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss; this paper studies accuracy as inference-time MCTS iterations increase.
Dependence of pretraining-law exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.
